question: Who competes with BSP for home-services deals?
html:
Home-Services Deal Competitors

BSP's main rivals for home-services deals are national HVAC and plumbing consolidators backed by larger sponsors. In Punctual Pros' PA/NJ market specifically, the active buyers are Sila (Goldman Sachs), Legacy Service Partners/HL Bowman (Gridiron), Ally Services (Watchtower) and Northwinds (TruArc) (Private-equity landscape).

Who sets add-on pricing

Residential services is the most crowded field on the map (Private-equity landscape). Six national consolidators set add-on pricing:

  • Apex (Alpine)
  • Wrench (LGP)
  • TurnPoint (OMERS)
  • Redwood (Altas)
  • Any Hour (Knox Lane)
  • T3 (Riverside)

BSP is also outsized on capital. Fund I is about $335M. Rival flagships run $0.9–2.1B, for example Trivest VII at $950M and Gridiron V at $2.1B (Private-equity landscape; BSP firm profile).

Local rivals by financial health

RivalSponsor or lenderPosition
Sila (King of Prussia)Goldman SachsHealthy. Est. $450–650M revenue (low confidence), built almost entirely by acquisition
Haller (Lancaster)Not statedHealthy. 254 trucks
Legacy/HL BowmanGridironScaled tier. Borrows at S+425–475, marked at par
Horizon ServicesLender-owned by 2026Stressed. At least $211M first lien at Blue Owl, 3.75% PIK, marked 92.5
HeartlandNot statedDebt matures Dec 15, 2026

Sources: Competitor filings; Home-services company case studies.

What this means for BSP

  • Scaled buyers are better funded. Lenders give the large consolidators par pricing and delayed-draw acquisition lines. The next tier (TurnPoint, Horizon, Any Hour, Len the Plumber) has moved to part-PIK interest and is marked at 89–94 (Competitor filings).
  • Two local rivals may become sellers. Horizon and Heartland are more likely to sell assets or restructure in the next 12 months than to bid hard for add-ons (Competitor filings). This is an analyst inference, not a confirmed event.
  • Exit valuations are high. Champions sold to Blackstone at a reported ~18.5x (Home-services company case studies).
  • Avoid auctions. BSP's suggested edge is the franchise system (Authority Brands territory rights, brand conversion) plus proprietary outreach to shops under $3M EBITDA that large-cap sponsors skip (Private-equity landscape).

Data gaps

  • Head-to-head losses. The context has no record of deals BSP lost or who won them. BSP's own pipeline and lost-deal log would answer this.
  • Add-on multiples. No local add-on multiples are given. Closed-deal comps for PA/NJ would answer this.
  • Haller's owner. Haller's sponsor, if any, is not identified.

Next actions

  1. Build a target list of Horizon and Heartland branches and assets in or next to Punctual Pros' counties. Time outreach to Heartland's Dec 15, 2026 maturity.
  2. Run a proprietary sourcing campaign for founder-owned shops under $3M EBITDA. Pitch Authority Brands brand conversion.
  3. Start a lost-deal tracker that records the winning bidder and multiple, so competitor pricing is measured rather than inferred.
  4. Map Sila's and Legacy's 2026 add-ons by county to see where Punctual Pros will face contested bids.
